title: Aperture: Social Media Downloader
summary: A clean, ad-free web app that saves reels, videos, photos and full carousels from Instagram, X, Facebook and Pinterest. Paste a link, pick a quality, keep the post: most links are ready in 2–4 seconds.
description: An open-source downloader built as an installable web app for Brave and mobile Chrome. A Node.js server runs yt-dlp and gallery-dl behind a strict host allowlist, merges audio with ffmpeg, streams live progress to a React interface, and deletes every file within minutes. The extractors stay loaded in a long-running Python worker, so lookups skip interpreter startup, and Instagram photos, carousels and videos are read from the same public data any logged-out visitor sees. A hosted scraper remains only as a backup for the rare post that cannot be read that way, so no personal account is ever used.
role: Sole developer. Product design, frontend, backend, security hardening and deployment.
visibility: Public web app and open-source repository (MIT).

methodology.title: Free path first, paid backup last
methodology.detail: yt-dlp handles video, quality selection and Instagram photos without logging in; gallery-dl adds photos on X, Facebook and Pinterest; an Apify backup is used only when Instagram cannot be read or hides a video's sound.

methodology.title: Speed found by measuring
methodology.detail: Profiling the live server showed lookups were slow because each one started fresh Python processes on a fraction of a CPU, not because of the network. Keeping the extractors loaded, skipping tools that cannot succeed and caching repeat links cut typical lookups from 10–70 seconds to 2–4.

methodology.title: Security before features
methodology.detail: Allowlisted hosts, no shell invocation, server-side ids instead of client URLs, CDN-restricted media, strict CSP, and per-visitor rate, size and duration limits.

methodology.title: Measured, not assumed
methodology.detail: Every platform was tested from the live server; ones that block cloud servers (YouTube, TikTok, Reddit) were removed from the public instance instead of being left to fail.

limitations: Platforms actively change their sites to stop downloaders, so no downloader works every time; extractors update daily to recover quickly.
Private posts, stories and deleted content cannot be downloaded without a logged-in account, which the public instance deliberately never uses; it runs on free hosting with daily usage caps.

title: Osho Documentary: Impartial Archival Inquiry
summary: An impartial, evidence-graded investigative inquiry into Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh (1931–1990) deconstructing his life, teachings, Oregon commune, 1984 bioterror attack, and global legacy.
description: An unflinching, evidence-graded documentary web archive examining Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh (Osho). Built from over 5,000 recorded audio discourses, declassified FBI vault dossiers, and Wasco County court exhibits, placing contradictory biographical and institutional accounts side by side with rigorous epistemic grading.
role: Creator and researcher. Archival curation, historical synthesis, and web development.
visibility: Public web documentary and archival research project.

methodology.title: Primary source corpus & FBI vault
methodology.detail: Cross-referenced thousands of audio discourses, Wasco County grand jury records, CDC reports, and declassified federal exhibits.

methodology.title: Evidence-graded chronology
methodology.detail: Structured across five investigative volumes (Life, Teachings, Movement, Controversies, Legacy) with interactive timeline and photo vault.

methodology.title: Contested claims side-by-side
methodology.detail: Keeps documented events distinct from interpretations and explicitly flags conflicting witness testimonies without premature adjudication.

limitations: Accounts of Osho and Rajneeshpuram are heavily polarized across memoirs, state prosecutions, and sannyasin accounts.
Secondary sources carry significant institutional and emotional biases; primary legal and audio evidence is given precedence.
